name: heron

attributes.attribute: symbolic waterbird that lived in air, land, and water and became an emblem of Otherworld power
appears in contexts like the cranes and typically represents the feminine force
tried to steal the herons of the fairy mound of Brí Léith, which stood for inhospitality

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The heron is a symbolic animal. Several bird species carried symbolic value in Celtic tradition. The heron was one of them. As a waterbird it lived in air, land, and water. It therefore became an emblem of Otherworld power. Herons appear in contexts like the cranes. They typically represent the feminine force. One story is an exception. The bitter satirist Aithirne tried to steal the herons of the fairy mound of Brí Léith. Those herons stood for the sin of inhospitality.
objective: Document the heron as a symbolic animal of Celtic tradition.
key_results: Record the heron as an emblem of Otherworld power as a waterbird.
Describe its parallel with the cranes and the feminine force.
Note Aithirne's attempt to steal the herons of Brí Léith.
evidence: Monaghan, P. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore (2008): heron entry.
